The profit decline was mainly attributable to a £179m provision charge in Q1-26 for historical motor finance commission payments and higher restructuring costs, only partially offset by TSB's £96m contribution. Management maintains guidance on net lending growth for 2026 and reiterates RoTE and cost synergies targets for 2028. Results reflect one-off charges rather than operational underperformance, with underlying business metrics improving.
